_readme: Which gates cover which files, for `discipline gate --changed`. `npm run gate` is unchanged and
always correct; this is the map that lets a change run a subset of it without losing coverage.
Edit it when your project grows a directory this map does not know: an unmapped file is not
ignored, it makes the FULL gate run, so the cost of an out-of-date map is time, never a missed check.
Scripts are npm script names and must exist in package.json. Every surface needs an entry, even an
empty one, because a surface nobody mentions is a gate nobody runs.
This lane ships no migrations, so `schema` maps to no path: it only ever arrives declared.
A surface MAY name a gate that `npm run gate` does not run (gate:visual). That is the point:
`npm run gate` cannot demand browser verification of every project, and this map only demands it
of a change that touched the UI. It needs the browsers installed (npm run e2e:install); a project
that does not verify UI in a browser takes gate:visual out of this file, deliberately, instead of
finding out it never ran. There is no test:rls here: the backend lives in a sidecar web app,
and that repo's own map owns its authenticated checks.
